events.title: Merry Making: Play, Build and Create With NVIDIA Technologies This Holiday Season
events.summary: The elves don’t have to be the only ones busy in the workshop this holiday season. With the lights twinkling and the gift wrap out, it’s the perfect time to give someone — or yourself — a spark to take a hobby to the next level. For some, that means diving into a new game. For others, it’s video editing or even building a robot. NVIDIA technologies offer something for everyone on Santa’s list. Read on to unwrap the details. With the holiday break here, everyone can be online to score bragging rights or explore a world that’s only been seen in video game trailers. For some players, an upgrade means a desktop that brings out the detail in every scene. For others, it’s a laptop they can take along when visiting family, or a way to play in the cloud on a device they already own. The right setup depends on where and what to play: GeForce RTX 50 Series laptops and desktops power the action. Built on the NVIDIA Blackwell architecture, they feature fifth-generation Tensor Cores and fourth-generation RT Cores for AI-enhanced graphics, detailed ray-traced worlds and high frames-per-second gaming. NVIDIA RTX Spark PCs combine RTX graphics with NVIDIA’s full-stack AI platform on a single superchip, bringing decades of NVIDIA innovation to slim, premium laptops and compact desktops on the familiar Windows platform. One PC can handle every workflow, from accelerated creation and immersive gaming to powerful local AI — with a variety of designs and all-day battery life. See games in a new light with NVIDIA DLSS 5 technology, which boosts performance and enhances image quality. The newest feature, DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, infuses scenes with lifelike lighting and materials in supported games. Get a glimpse of NBA 2K27 with DLSS 5 . NVIDIA Reflex and G-SYNC make gameplay more responsive and fluid. Reflex reduces system latency in supported games, while G-SYNC displays use variable refresh rates to deliver smooth, tear-free gaming. The GeForce NOW cloud gaming service enables playing top titles anywhere. Stream supported games on compatible laptops, TVs, handhelds and more. Connect to supported game stores to play owned PC games, with more than 4,500 titles available across the service. For creators with a project that’s been on the backburner, the right gift this season can be the push to finally make it happen. Maybe it’s holiday clips becoming a short film, a snowy scene coming together in 3D or a livestream that brings friends across time zones to the same virtual table. Creators can use NVIDIA systems — such as GeForce RTX 50 Series and RTX Spark devices — to keep up with the workflows, along with NVIDIA Studio tools and technologies for AI acceleration. Studio Drivers support video editing, 3D design and livestreaming. In supported applications, faster processing gives more room to experiment and refine. Every robot starts somewhere. This season, it could be under the tree. Building a robot is an experiment in teaching a device to see or sense its surroundings. A first project might be as simple as using a camera to identify a candy cane or a gingerbread man, then moving on to an app that probes what the camera sees. Testing brings new questions. Can the robot recognize the candy cane under twinkling lights? Can it tell a frosted gingerbread man from an unfrosted one? Each experiment leaves more to improve and explore. The NVIDIA Jetson edge AI platform provides the hardware and software to build projects like these. It combines compact computers with the NVIDIA JetPack software development kit to help makers build robots, autonomous machines and intelligent devices. A Jetson Developer Kit is a gift to explore computer vision, generative AI and multimodal robot control, with the option to add cameras and sensors suited to various projects. AI runs directly on the device, processing information from its surroundings. When ready to take a prototype further, production systems powered by Jetson modules provide a path to deployment. See how Microduck comes to life with NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super , bringing together robot movement, visual understanding and natural-language interaction. With Hermes Agent and NVIDIA Cosmos, developers can explore how AI connects everyday requests with actions in the physical world. events.title: Kandoo Car Credit Ltd enters administration
events.summary: On 19 November 2026, Kandoo Car Credit Ltd (Kandoo) was placed into administration. Steve Kenny and Richard Cole of KBL Advisory Limited were appointed as joint administrators. Kandoo Car Credit (firm reference number 936619) operated as a motor finance credit broker arranging finance for consumers purchasing vehicles from third-party car dealerships. The joint administrators, Steve Kenny and Richard Cole of KBL Advisory Ltd, are now responsible for Kandoo while it is in administration. If you have questions about the administration or a claim against Kandoo, contact the joint administrators.Email: kandoo.queries@kbl-advisory.comKandoo is no longer arranging finance. If you have an existing loan agreement arranged by Kandoo, your agreement is with your lender, not Kandoo. Continue making repayments to your lender as usual. If you have not received your vehicle, a payment has not reached the dealership, or you are unsure about the status of your agreement, contact your lender and the joint administrators to discuss your circumstances.If your finance arrangements are still being completed, you have not collected your vehicle, or you are seeking to unwind your agreement, contact your lender and the joint administrators directly. Explain what has happened, including any payments you have made, so they can clarify the status of your agreement and the next steps.Kandoo has told us it has no open motor finance complaints. The joint administrators will ensure this information is correct. Kandoo remains liable for any compensation it owes. Contact your lender about a scheme claim, and the joint administrators about a claim against Kandoo itself.Since becoming aware of Kandoo’s financial difficulties, we have worked to protect consumers’ interests. Customers who have claims directly against Kandoo may be affected by the administration. This is separate from compensation payable under our scheme, for which responsibility rests with the relevant lender. Protect yourself from scamsAll customers should remain alert to the possibility of fraud.If you receive an unexpected phone call from someone claiming to be from Kandoo, the joint administrators or the FCA, end the call. Contact the organisation using details you have independently checked, rather than a number or link supplied by the caller.Find out more about protecting yourself from scams.If you're looking for an alternative firm to arrange finance on a vehicle, you should only deal with firms authorised by us. If you're unsure whether a firm is authorised, use the FCA Firm Checker.

events.title: Jensen Huang Is Back as Nvidia CEO
events.summary: Jensen Huang is stepping back into his role as chief executive of Nvidia effective immediately. The stunning reversal comes 11 days after Huang resigned as CEO from the company he cofounded 33 years ago and after multiple declarations from the board of directors that it had no intention of reinstating him. On Monday, they took a conciliatory tone. “The Board believes Jensen is the right person to lead Nvidia and that his reinstatement is in the best interests of our stockholders, employees, partners, and customers,” said recently appointed board chair Harvey Jones in a press release announcing the decision. In that announcement the board said it was “satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia” and that it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” on the way to its decision. On Monday morning, President Donald Trump posted that the Nvidia board “has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO.” “I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution,” said Huang in a statement. “I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment.” Huang resigned as Nvidia’s CEO on November 12, and longtime chief financial officer Colette Kress was installed as his interim replacement. Five days later, Huang publicly announced that he was open to resuming his role as chief executive, noting the “outpouring of calls” from “employees, investors, business partners, and customers” advocating for his return. “If the board of directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO,” Huang wrote. The day Huang resigned, many Nvidia employees spoke up in his support. As reported by WIRED, employees left more than 1,600 comments on an internal “suggestion box” post in which they urged the company’s board to reinstall him as CEO. In the days following, a public petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement began circulating. At the time of writing, it has amassed more than 200,000 online signatures, the majority of whom self-identified as Nvidia shareholders. Tech elites like Elon Musk and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan have claimed that they were going to sign the petition or had signed it. Huang’s reinstatement marks a total reversal from the public stance of Nvidia’s board of directors, which said during the company’s November 17 earnings call that it “does not intend” to reinstate him as CEO. WIRED has further reported that the board was alarmed by what one source described as Huang’s “lying” over the last year or so. President Donald Trump, who developed a close working relationship with Huang during his second administration, had indicated openness to Huang returning as CEO. Trump told reporters on November 16 that he “would not mind” if Huang returned as chief executive, adding that he believed he had “learned a big lesson.” Huang’s resignation followed days of scrutiny over several extramarital romantic relationships: one with Chinese businesswoman Alice Huang, who has no known relation to Jensen, one with an Nvidia employee who directly reported to Huang, and one with a different Nvidia employee. Huang’s relationship with Alice became the subject of particularly intense focus on November 6, when The New York Times and Financial Times reported that US intelligence officials suspected that Alice may be an asset of the Chinese Ministry of State Security, both citing an intelligence briefing that circulated among top Trump administration officials last year. In the days since, some reports and Trump administration officials have questioned the accuracy of that intelligence. The Chinese government has consistently rejected claims that Alice was one of its spies. Alice was the chief executive of Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI company that’s been accused of helping Chinese tech companies use Nvidia’s most advanced chips at overseas locations, effectively sidestepping US export restrictions. Alice has also reportedly worked as a television reporter, at HSBC’s Hong Kong-based private banking arm , and at an investment bank backed by the Chinese state. Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 with Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem, purportedly with the mission of bringing realistic 3D graphics to personal computers. For many years, the company was primarily known within the gaming community . It didn’t become a household name until the recent AI boom, when its graphics processing units (GPUs) became a crucial piece of infrastructure for powering advanced AI models. Nvidia controlled about 90 percent of the global GPU market as of September 2026. The year prior, it became the first company to be valued at more than $4 trillion, though its stock price has been in precipitous decline since Huang’s resignation.

events.title: Nvidia reinstates former CEO Jensen Huang despite China espionage scandal
events.summary: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO despite China scandal Nvidia's board voted unanimously to bring back the disgraced CEO, who resigned this month amid news of his affairs. He's suspected of having had a relationship with a Chinese intelligence asset. US tech company Nvidia said on Monday that it had reinstated Jensen Huang as its CEO "effective immediately." This follows just a matter of days after his resignation after admitting to extramarital affairs, reportedly including a dalliance with a woman who was a Chinese intelligence asset. What did Nvidia and Huang say about the move? The board unanimously decided that his return was in the "best interests of the company," Nvidia said, adding that it was satisfied that Huang had demonstrated his "candor and ability to lead." Meanwhile, the 63-year-old said in a statement that he was "honored" to return to the company and that he would take on the renewed responsibility "with the greatest humility and renewed commitment." He thanked interim CEO Colette Kress , who is set to return to her role as chief financial officer. "I am also deeply thankful to our employees, shareholders, leaders across the industry and partners around the world for their extraordinary support," Huang said. "Above all, I am grateful for the love and support of my family. I can't wait to get back to work." US President Donald Trump rapidly commented on the development online, saying it was the "correct and proper decision" and referring to Huang by his first name as a "Great Patriot and National Treasure." "The United States Government has no reason to believe that Jensen's return to Nvidia poses any risk to National Security," Trump wrote, also saying that the US had no evidence of him engaging in unlawful conduct. Huang liked to flaunt his personal relationship with Trump. He was reportedly influential in convincing the US president to allow the export of higher-quality Nvidia chips to China that are useful in AI development than other US officials and entrepreneurs endorsed. Nvidia stock volatility continues, with spike after announcement The decision was announced as trading started for the new week in New York. The stock price of what investors deem the world's most valuable company has nosedived amid the scandal, with Nvidia's stock price falling from almost $220 (roughly €200) per share in late October to around $125 per share at the end of last week. The announcement prompted a rapid early-morning rally on Wall Street, including Nvidia stocks rising back into a region between $160 and $170. Anthropic raises $81 billion in record-breaking IPO Huang quit earlier this month after admitting to extramarital affairs in a note to employees. This concession came amid widespread reporting in the US linking him romantically to one woman in particular, who was running a major Nvidia client called Megaspeed based in Singapore and who was said to be an asset of Chinese intelligence services. Her company is also suspected of diverting chips not approved for export to China to the Chinese market, circumventing US sanctions. While these allegations have not been proven, they appeared to be based on the assessments of US and other western intelligency agencies, and to be information that was known for around a year. One possible indication of this was Singapore refusing the Chinese national entry into the country earlier in 2026.
